long_biography.plain_text:
After completing economics studies at St Gallen and publishing training in the United States, Dieter von Holtzbrinck joined Handelsblatt as a managing partner in 1970. He later took over leadership of the family media business from his father. He redirected proceeds from the book-club operation into international growth and widened the newspaper portfolio by acquiring Die Zeit.

Von Holtzbrinck left executive management before selling his original family-company stake to his siblings. In 2009, he used financial claims from that exit to take control of Handelsblatt and Tagesspiegel, together with half of Die Zeit. He placed those assets in a newly established holding company. Professional executives handle operations; he influences strategy and editorial values through his continuing ownership role.

Deutsche Biographie gives the authority form Georg Dieter von Holtzbrinck and Welthungerhilfe uses Georg-Dieter, while public business sources consistently use Dieter von Holtzbrinck. Because the canonical record already uses Dieter as the first name, inserting Georg as a middle name would reverse the authority-record order. No name-field correction is proposed.

Forbes documents his 2006 sale of the original family-group stake and the 2009 exchange of remaining claims for newspaper assets. Classifications therefore rest on his inherited stake, documented expansion and continuing DvH Medien shareholding, not on assets currently held by Stefan von Holtzbrinck or Christiane Schoeller.
